why: a constructor allocates the instance with each field's default, stores its parameter properties and field initializers in declaration order, then runs its body: Meter's reading initializer changes but the body stores over it (proved, and metered with it); Gauge's level initializer changes and nothing stores over it (WITNESS); Span (parameter properties only) is untouched, span hands its arguments swapped (WITNESS); Cell stores its count through a local after its parameter properties (proved, and sized with it); Square calls super with the same value written differently (proved, and perimeter with it); Triangle calls super with another value (WITNESS); Shape is untouched; kept calls bumped on a Tally it built and used only through its fields, where the candidate writes the count itself (proved: an exact, unshared instance runs Tally's own text); handed gives the Tally to an outside function before the call, and relayed to Tally's own shared, which hands this to it: the outside function installs an own bumped on the instance (WITNESS, unproved: once the instance is shared, its method may be another function)
